skills.summary: Turn any public website into a branded video: capture, storyboard, voice, sound and editable motion layers.

examples.caption: 1. Site tour: subclip.app captured, brand sheet, its own headline, 200+ templates, call to action. Rendered in code, no video model.
2. Brand sheet: colors, font and logo read from the captured page. Rendered in code, no image model.
3. Trail tour: a field guide's captured map pushes in behind a two-line opener.
4. Trail close-up: the site's own contour map shows how to spot the ridge.

skills.examplesCredit: Test outputs made with this skill in Subclip. Rendered in code (HyperFrames layers): no image, video or audio model. Site tour music: Angel-techno pop music loop by frankum, CC BY 4.0.

installYourself.name: Kubai Icons
installYourself.what: An agent skill that draws icons in one consistent style, with hover motion. Three looks (layered, two-tone solid and line), 4,800+ ready icons for React, Vue and plain SVG, and a website to browse them.
installYourself.why: Its source-available license lets you install and use it, also for paid work, and the icons you draw are yours. It does not allow sharing a changed version, so Subclip cannot adapt it. Install the original yourself, export your icons as SVG files or record their hover motion on its gallery page, then import them into Subclip.

installYourself.name: Idol

references.group: Access needed before the first run

installYourself.what: Turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat (.ply file), including the sides the picture never showed. A Python inference SDK and a local demo app, best on an NVIDIA GPU with about 8 GB of memory.
installYourself.why: Does not work inside Subclip. It is not a video editing skill: it needs a local Python and GPU setup and makes 3D Gaussian splats, which Subclip cannot load as a 3D layer. Install it yourself (pip install -e .), run python -m idol.sample on your image, turn the result in its demo viewer or any splat viewer, record that as a video and import it into Subclip.
